einstellungen.text: Someone needs a doctor right now. And not a single phone in the world works.
Grandpa's breathing is shallow. Lina is holding his hand. Ben is pacing in circles.
You go to dial the emergency number. Out of habit. No bars.
Then the old radio man opens up his set. “Stay calm. This is what this is for.”
During big outages, ham radio operators help pass messages along. No network needed.
His call goes from operator to operator. Right across the city. All the way to the fire department.
Then it crackles. “Ambulance is on the way. Ten minutes.”
Ten minutes can be a very long time. Grandpa squeezes your hand. Very weakly.
Then you see it. Flashing blue lights. In the middle of a city with no lights.
The hospital runs on emergency power. Big generators in the basement that kick in when the grid goes down.
The doctors are working with paper and ballpoint pens. Like the old days.
And then the door opens. Mom. Dad. The radio man's note found them.
Mom doesn't say a word. She just holds on to you. Both of you.
Dad sits down next to Grandpa. “We should have come so much more often.”
The doctor says: he's stable. You can stay.
Through the window, you watch the sky slowly turn green.
The second storm is here. And all over the hospital, the lights go out.
